newsitem.title: USA: Riot police halt L.A. protest against ex-Klan head.
newsitem.headline: Riot police halt L.A. protest against ex-Klan head.

text.p: Police in riot gear on Wednesday broke up an unruly demonstration at a suburban university campus against a visit by former Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke for a debate on affirmative action.
Several people were arrested at California State University at Northridge after about 200 protesters opposing Duke clashed with a smaller group of his supporters, police said.

Dozens of police officers, some on horseback, used batons and "flash-bang" percussion devices to disperse the crowd after fighting erupted outside the student union building where Duke and Los Angeles civil rights activist Joe Hicks held a public debate.
A few demonstrators pelted police with rocks, and several people were injured. "Go home, KKK," some protesters chanted. "Death to fascists," one woman yelled.

Duke, an avowed white supremacist who has served in the Louisiana legislature and made unsuccessful bids for the U.S. Senate, was in Los Angeles to speak out against affirmative action -- programmes that give preference to women, blacks and other minorities in hiring, education and business.

But the visit by Duke, who was invited and paid an appearance fee by the university's student government, angered many students and minority activists opposed to giving him a forum to express his views.

Some of the harhest criticism of Duke's appearance came from supporters of Proposition 209, the Nov. 5 California ballot initiative that calls for outlawing affirmative action programmes by state and local government agencies. Backers of the measure say Duke was invited as a ploy to discredit the initiative through association with his extremist views.
Inside the college auditorium, the debate was briefly interrupted when a man charged the stage shouting "racist" at Duke. Police grabbed the protester and removed him.
Speaking to an audience of more than 500, Duke claimed affirmative action "discriminates against white people in jobs, promotions, scholarships, college admissions and loan programmes."

But Hicks responded with ridicule. "It's the cry of every unqualified white guy who ever gets aced out of a job because they don't want to admit that out there are some minority folks and some women who've got better qualifications," he said.
